summary: While FIX and EME compounded on data centers, Limbach stayed singularly focused on owner direct work and ended up with effectively zero data center exposure. I push back on the bear case that management knowingly bid a pile of low margin work, on whether owner direct is just general contracting by another name, on whether wage inflation from the data cente Receivables are up 120% against 45% revenue growth.

thesis: This episode argues that winning a stock pitch competition relies more on extensive legwork and understanding durable growth stories than on complex financial modeling. It highlights specific opportunities in companies like DoorDash, Liberty Global, and Stevanato where management teams believe the market is mispricing long-term potential due to overlooked verticals, spin-offs, or switching costs.

claims.claim: Aurelian Research's Leo Trudel argues that fears of oral GLP-1s replacing injectables are a misread because biologics demand keeps growing and switching costs are real.
claims.quote: Stevanato (STVN) makes the glass vials and pre-filled syringes that GLP-1 drugs ship in. The stock has sold off on fears that oral GLP-1s replace injectables, but Aurelian Research's Leo Trudel argues that's a misread: biologics demand keeps growing, the mix is shifting toward higher-margin "high-value solutions," and switching costs in regulated drug delivery are real.
